description: Score a finished sweep (harness2-judge): the judge model grades the selected run of every task and mode against the benchmark's criteria into judged.json, or with bases=true the reference executions on the unmodified harness into base_judged.json. Calls the judge model: COSTS MONEY with cloud models. Use exactly the run's identity — same experiment, cell (bench, subset, substrate), k, seed and modes — and the experiment's profile, or nothing matches. Operator role. Ungraded rows (judge failures, no pick) are counted separately and are NOT zeros. Returns the queued job; follow with wait_for_job, then get_report.

description: Start the whole workflow as one job: preview, check, run, judge (and judge the base executions when judge_bases=true), report; it stops at the first step that neither succeeds nor ends partial. Same inputs, COST WARNING and acknowledge_risks rule as start_run (executor, improver and judge models are called): get the user's go-ahead after preview_run and estimate_cost, set budget_usd, and set judge_bases=true so the report can compare against the unmodified harness. Operator role. Returns the queued job; follow with wait_for_job (pipelines run for a long time), then get_report for the sweep (the run step's result.namespace is the sweep id).

acknowledge_risks.description: Needed when the server runs jobs without container isolation (server_info shows isolation host): the executor then has the server user's files and network. description: Start a refinement sweep (harness2): per task, Propose-Probe-Compose recursion edits the agent harness (system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, sub-agents, skills, scripts, plugins), runs the executor and a blind selector adopts one harness. CALLS MODELS AND COSTS MONEY with cloud models (per task and mode up to 4k rollouts and 3k improver sessions). First run preview_run and estimate_cost and get the user's go-ahead; set budget_usd (it caps recorded improver spend; executor spend is not recorded). profile must be the experiment's pinned profile. Under host isolation the server needs acknowledge_risks=true (the executor gets the server user's files and network); this MCP server accepts it only when started with --allow-risk-acknowledgement, otherwise the user starts such runs in the web UI. Operator role. Returns the queued job; follow with wait_for_job, then start_judge with the same cell, k, seed and modes — or use start_pipeline.

description: Change an experiment's description, tags or archived flag (operator role); arguments you leave out stay as they are. tags replaces the whole tag list. archived=true hides the experiment from list_experiments (include_archived shows it again) without deleting anything on disk; archived=false restores it. The pinned profile and the results cannot be changed here. Returns the updated experiment.

archived.description: `true` archives the experiment (hidden from default listings, nothing deleted); `false` restores it; absent = unchanged.

description: Validate a harness tree against harness2's own rules (the checks applied to improver proposals) without running anything. Pass the surface (opencode or codex), every file's relative path and content, and allow_subagents=false for deployments that forbid sub-agents (upstream: LAB). Returns ok, harness2's actionable error messages, files outside the editable surface (ignored by harness2) and the census (always-on characters vs the cap). Use it for hand-edited harnesses or raw exports before using them.

description: Wait until a job finishes, up to timeout_secs (default 50, max 600). Follows the server's job events (polling as a fallback) and sends MCP progress notifications with task progress (done/total, current task) when your client supplies a progress token. Returns the job (as get_job) once it is succeeded, partial, failed or cancelled — or, on timeout, the job as it is now with a note; call again to keep waiting (sweeps can take hours). Waiting changes nothing on the server. If your client cuts tool calls off after a fixed time (often 60 s), keep timeout_secs below it.

job_id.description: Job id (returned by the tool that started the job, or from list_jobs).

poll_interval_secs.description:
Seconds between status checks when the server's event stream is unavailable (default
2).

timeout_secs.description:
Longest time to wait, in seconds (default 50, max 600). On timeout the job is returned
as it is and keeps running.

name: wait_for_job
title: Wait for a job
